name: Tiramisu (savoiardi base)
origin: A no-bake Italian dessert first documented in the Veneto in the 1960s-1970s; layers of coffee- and liqueur-soaked savoiardi (ladyfinger sponge fingers) with a whipped mascarpone-and-egg cream, dusted with cocoa.

ingredients.note: yolk and white whipped separately then combined, as in a genoise, but stiffer and piped into finger shapes

process.name: whip yolks and sugar
process.description: whip egg yolks with half the sugar until pale and thick

process.name: whip whites
process.description: whip egg whites with the remaining sugar to a stiff, stable meringue

process.name: fold together and pipe
process.description: fold the yolk mixture and sifted flour into the meringue, then pipe into finger shapes

process.name: bake
process.description: bake until just set and lightly golden

notes: This formulation deliberately covers only savoiardi, tiramisu's one genuinely baked component — a stiff, egg-rich, fat-free foam sponge (no butter or oil at all, correctly zero here). The mascarpone-egg cream, coffee soak, liqueur and cocoa dusting that make the finished dessert are a no-bake custard-and-cream assembly, a different physical process from a baked batter (no starch gelatinisation, no protein coagulation under heat) and are described only narratively, out of scope for the baker's-percentage formulation here — the same reasoning documented in catalog.ts's blockers for the excluded cheesecakes, applied correctly by scoping the formulation to only the part of tiramisu that really is a baked cake.
